name: Phinehas
overview: Phinehas was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known primarily as the son of Eli, a corrupt priest. His role and character are noted in the context of his priestly lineage. No additional personal notes are provided in the source material.
namesAndTitles: The name Phinehas means 'the black man.' This is the only recorded name for him, and it is not indicated to have been given by God. The meaning provides a cultural or descriptive insight but no further theological significance is noted.
familyAndRelationships: Phinehas is explicitly identified as the son of Eli, who served as a priest. It is also inferred that he was the father of Ichabod and Ahitub, indicating a generational priestly lineage. These relationships highlight his place within a family connected to the Levitical priesthood.
scriptureSignificance: Phinehas's significance in Scripture is tied to his identity as the son of Eli, whose corrupt priesthood sets a backdrop for Phinehas's own role within the Levitical tribe. His familial connections suggest a continuation of the priestly line during a turbulent period in Israel's history. While the text does not elaborate on his personal actions, his lineage situates him within the unfolding narrative of Israel's priesthood.
